data.independent_check: A closure contact alone does not ensure an accessible common boundary point. This is why the necessary finite-chain condition was not promoted to an equivalence.
data.method: Reduction to component adjacency and access
data.obstruction: Need finite accessible chains for every pair of components, simultaneously for the Brownian trace.
data.result: If both endpoints lie in the same component of the complement of the Brownian trace, an open connected planar set is polygonally connected; removing loops gives a simple arc avoiding the trace entirely. If an arc crosses the trace finitely many times, its complementary intervals give a finite sequence of complement components with touching closures at successive crossing points.

data.independent_check: For each deterministic s, {s<T} is measurable from the segment up to s. Future Brownian increments followed by independent stopped segments retain the Brownian law and are independent of the past. Integrating over s gives a Brownian future under Q; stationarity then supplies a Brownian past and its independence. This is a proof outline pending full artifact and earlier-literature comparison, not a newly claimed theorem.
data.method: Stationary Palm construction in the identically distributed finite-mean case
data.obstruction: The actual question allows independent non-identically distributed segments. There is then no invariant iid index law or common Palm mean to which this argument applies.
data.result: For iid stopped Brownian segments with 0<E T<infinity, the cycle sequence is ergodic under shifting its index. A stationary occupation law is Q(F)=E[integral_0^T F(theta_s X) ds]/E T. Shifting by t changes the numerator by E[integral_T^(T+t) F(theta_s X) ds-integral_0^t F(theta_s X) ds]=0 because the concatenation rooted at the next cycle has the same Palm law. Tilting the iid cycle sequence by T_0/E T and choosing a uniform time in that cycle realizes this law; the forward filling lemma supplies that tilt by a finite randomized index shift.

data.independent_check: Independence of two halves at a proposed joining time is insufficient if their Brownian marginal laws have been lost there.
data.obstruction: No construction aligns both certificates at one time while preserving both marginal laws and their independence.
data.result: Two independent standard Brownian half-paths attached at the same deterministic time give a two-sided Brownian motion. For a general process certified separately as forward and backward Brownian, the certifying random times can differ. Moving either certificate to another random time can bias its marginal law, as the selection-density calculation in P0032 demonstrates.

data.independent_check: Restriction of an insertion tableau to labels at most b is the tableau of the corresponding restricted subword. The last specified first-row entry b pins the first k labels, irrespective of later larger labels. Conditional on B, the Poisson arrival times have independent gamma increments, so every term is a normalized conditional density and nonnegative summation is valid. For k1 this gives Exp(1); known Poissonized LIS formulas give P(X2>x)=exp(-x)*I0(2sqrt(x)) and E X2=e.
data.method: Explicit stationary law of the leftmost Hammersley drift-jump particles structural calculation
data.obstruction: This repackages a known representation into explicit but rapidly growing finite-tableau coefficients and an infinite sum. It does not establish a new tractable closed joint law or its novelty, and should not be promoted as a full solution to the source request.
data.result: The established rank representation can be expanded into a convergent combinatorial density series. Let B=(1=b1<...<bk) be the limiting first-row labels of the insertion tableau, and let q_B be its probability. The first b=bk labels form a uniform permutation, so q_B=(1/b!)*sum over partitions lambda of b with first row length k of f^lambda times the number of standard tableaux of shape lambda with first row B. Independent unit-rate Poisson spacings then give density exp(-xk)*sum_B q_B*product_(i=2..k)[(x_i-x_(i-1))^(b_i-b_(i-1)-1)/(b_i-b_(i-1)-1)!].

data.independent_check: The quadratic identity follows by E[I(m-I)]=m*(m-1)/(2H_(m-1)). The Colless bound uses only the exact clade-count identity and the established mean continuous leaf-depth theorem. It does not rely on the false unrestricted occupation ansatz.
data.method: Exact tree identity, source-specific recurrence or explicit limiting obstruction
data.obstruction: The mean Colless correction and one-split quadratic correction do not identify variances, normalized laws or joint distributions of the balance indices. Those remain unsolved here.
data.result: For a split I distributed by q(m,i), the exact quadratic toll is E(m-2I)^2=m^2-2m*(m-1)/H_(m-1), hence asymptotic to m^2 rather than the source m^2/4. Also E min(I,m-I)<=m/H_(m-1), so E|m-2I|=m-O(m/log m), rather than m/2. If S is the external path length and C the Colless index, S-C is the sum of2*min(child sizes). Therefore E(S-C)<=2n*sum_m a(n,m)/H_(m-1)=2n*E continuous leaf depth=O(n log n). Since E S~(3/pi^2)n log^2 n, E C has that same leading constant, twice the source heuristic coefficient.

data.statement: Almost surely, can every two points outside the trace of planar Brownian motion on [0,1] be connected by a Jordan arc meeting the trace at only finitely many points?
data.statement_caveat: The quantifier is simultaneous over all pairs of outside points, not a single deterministic pair.
data.title: Finite-crossing arcs through a planar Brownian trace

data.statement: Concatenate independent Brownian path segments cut at stopping times indexed by all integers, with lengths uniformly bounded by a deterministic constant and divergent sums in both directions. Is the resulting path two-sided Brownian after some random time shift?
data.statement_caveat: The paper's related backward-Brownian question and its almost-sure random bound are recorded as related variants, not an extra count. Independent lengths alone are not the same as stopping times depending on their Brownian paths.
data.title: Bounded independent Brownian pieces and two-sided Brownian motion

data.statement: Given a process whose law on nonnegative time is equivalent to Wiener measure, can a random finite prefix be added, on an enlarged probability space if necessary, to produce a process with Wiener law?
data.statement_caveat: No independence or Brownian stopping-time restriction is explicit in the source. The candidate proof uses a finite nonnegative integer random time depending on entire paths and auxiliary randomness.
data.title: Embedding an equivalent Brownian law by adding a finite prefix
